question.text: This capital of Poland sits on the Vistula and contains a statue of its coat of arms, a mermaid brandishing a sword, in its Old Town Market Place.
question.clue: Willy Brandt made a "knee-fall" in front of a monument in this city.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Eastern European leaders.
swap.text: Elected president of Poland in 1990, this man is famous for organizing the famous Soviet trade union, Solidarity.
swap.clue: His wife, Danuta, claimed his Nobel Peace Prize for him in 1983.

question.text: This trade union was created during the Lenin Shipyards strike. The actions of this trade union led to the fall of communism in Poland.
question.clue: This group helped remove Secretary Kania and Wojciech Jaruzelski from power, and the Gdansk Agreement and the Roundtable Talks eventually led to a leader of this group being elected as Prime Minister in 1989.

swap.text: The szlachta paralyzed this Polish-Lithuanian parliament with the liberum veto, which allowed singular noblemen to stop the legislative process.
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.leadin: Name these Europeans who served in the Continental Army.
question.text: This Polish military engineer created defenses for the Americans at the Battle of Saratoga. He led a namesake uprising against Russia during the Third Partition of Poland.
question.clue: This man better known for fortifying Saratoga against Burgyone and becoming the chief of the engineering corps during the American Revolutionary War.

swap.leadin: These events would bring about the end of the Polish Lithuanian Commonwealth.
swap.text: Name these political splittings of Poland Lithuania that took place in the late 18th century. In these events, Prussia, Austria, and Russia invaded and took land, to little resistance.
swap.clue: The three aforementioned treaties dividing Poland are commonly referred to by this term. Another treaty referred to by this term divided British India.

question.text: In March 1939, this previously East Prussian land east of the Memel River was returned to Germany from this country, after Joachim von Ribbentrop signed the Treaty of the Cession of the Memel Territory to Germany with Juozas Urbsys. It became a republic of the Soviet Union in 1944.
question.clue: This country's major port is Klaipeda, and its capital was nicknamed "Jeruzale" for its large Jewish population.

swap.leadin: An underground trade union in this country went on strike at the Lenin shipyards in Gdansk ("g-DA-eensk").
swap.text: Name this country. Lech Walesa ("lek va-WEN-sa") became this country's first post-communist president, but he lost re-election to Alexander Kwasniewski ("kfash-NEV-skee").
swap.clue: A Senate was created here after the 1989 Round Table Agreement.

question.leadin: William Wilkinson was brought in from England to manage one of the burgeoning iron works in the early 19th century in this region.
question.text: Identify this region that was secured by Prussia following a successful defense of Chotusitz (KHO-too-zits) in 1742 during the War of Austrian Succession, which ended with Maria Theresa losing it to Prussia.
question.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about anti-communist unrest in Poland.
swap.text: Solidarity's leader at the 1981 Gdansk shipyards protests was this man, who later became the first democratically elected president of Poland after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
swap.clue: The KOR ("K-O-R") was a predecessor to an organization led by this man, which formed a coalition government with the PUWP.

question.text: The Janissary Revolt of 1622 followed a disastrous defeat at Choczim against this country, a combined commonwealth of two modern-day states ruled by the Jagiellon dynasty, with which the Ottomans had fought the Moldavian Magnate Wars. They often fought over Tatar and Cossack raids.
question.clue: This state lost one-third of its population during the Swedish Deluge, and this union formed after Duke Jogaila ] married Queen Jadwiga ].

swap.text: Frederick created an elite unit of cavalry of this name, described by the word "totenkopf," or death's head.
swap.clue: Jan Sobieski led a decisive charge of these cavalrymen into the Ottoman line during the 1683 Siege of Vienna.

question.text: Under the command of Edigu and Temur Qutlugh ("KUT-lug"), the Horde won a victory over this state at the Battle of the Vorskla River. This state was led by Grand Duke Vytautas, who was a successor to Jogaila ("yo-GAI-wa").
question.answerHtml: Grand Duchy of Lithuania [accept Kingdom of Lithuania; reject “Poland-Lithuania” or “Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania” or “Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth”]
question.clue: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.

swap.text: At Grunwald, the Lithuanian forces were led by this Grand Duke of Lithuania. The Ostrow Agreement between this man and his cousin Jogaila ended the Lithuanian Civil War.
swap.clue: This junior partner in the Ostrow ("AW-stroof") Agreement sent his nephew Prince Korybut to rule the Hussites.

question.leadin: During this country's resistance to Russification, the Knygnesiai, or Book Smugglers, promoted its native language.
question.text: Identify this country that joined Poland in the Union of Lublin and whose capital is Vilnius.
question.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

swap.text: The legendary first king of Poland had this name, which is also the first name of the twentieth-century politician who co-founded Solidarity and won the Nobel Peace Prize.
swap.clue: Sarmatism was often combined with the myth that the Poles were descendants of this figure, one of three legendary founders of the Slavic peoples. This son of Pan reached Poland after following a white eagle to its nest.

question.text: The "Galician Slaughter" of 1846 was directed at Polish nobles who were revolting in this nearby city, which had been made a "Free City" at the Congress of Vienna. The 1794 Kosciuszko Uprising started in this city.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.text: This man was the last Jagiellonian king to rule Poland. He oversaw the height of the Polish Reformation and expanded his kingdom into Livonia and Russia.
swap.clue: The election of Henry of Valois followed the 1572 death of this Polish king, the last of the Jagellon dynasty. He himself was succeded by Stephen Bathory, who brought the Livonian War to a conclusion.

question.leadin: Sadly for this man, he ordered his victorious forces not to destroy the enemy army at the battle of Stegeborg to reduce the massacre.
question.text: Name this Catholic who was then soundly defeated at the battle of Stangebro by his uncle Duke Charles, who stripped him of one of his thrones in 1599, though he continued to rule Poland for quite a while.
question.answerHtml: Sigismund III Vasa [or Sigismund of Sweden; prompt on partial answers]
question.clue: This ruler and his cousin signed a peace treaty at Altmark that was extended by this ruler's son at Stuhmsdorf.

swap.text: Boleslav was one of the great rulers of this dynasty which was founded by Mieszko I and whose other notable monarchs include Boleslav II and Casimir I.
swap.clue: The semi-legendary namesake of this dynasty was a wheelwright who was legendarily visited by two angels in disguise who blessed his cellar.
